7.text:
Cyberbullying, online scams, false news and loneliness are regularly blamed on the internet, and some argue that it is the main reason for social problems. I disagree to a large extent, since the internet magnifies social problems but rarely creates them, and its benefits are also considerable.

To begin with, the internet magnifies social problems but rarely creates them. Bullying, misinformation and isolation existed before, and the internet makes them faster and more visible, while the underlying causes are poverty, family breakdown and weak education. A false rumour about a neighbour, for example, once spread slowly by gossip but can now reach thousands in minutes. This amplification is serious, since victims may face abuse at any hour, but the roots of the behaviour lie in human attitudes and social conditions, not in cables and servers. Crime, inequality, addiction and discrimination all existed long before the internet and still exist in places where few people are online.

Furthermore, the internet also helps to solve social problems. It allows isolated people to find communities, helps victims to report abuse, gives access to education and health information, and enables campaigns for change. During crises, such as pandemics, online tools kept schools, businesses and families connected. However, it would be wrong to ignore real harm. Algorithms that reward outrage can increase division, and heavy use may affect the wellbeing of some young people. Governments and platforms should therefore regulate harmful content, protect children and teach digital skills, while also tackling the social conditions that make people vulnerable. Without addressing these deeper causes, restricting the internet alone would solve little.

In conclusion, the internet is not the main reason for social problems, because it mostly amplifies difficulties that have other causes, although it can aggravate them and needs sensible regulation.

Ví dụ tin đồn sai về hàng xóm từng lan chậm qua buôn chuyện nay đến hàng nghìn người trong vài phút. Gốc của hành vi nằm ở thái độ và điều kiện xã hội; tội phạm, bất bình đẳng, nghiện, phân biệt có từ trước internet và vẫn tồn tại ở nơi ít người online.

Internet cũng giúp giải quyết vấn đề xã hội: người cô lập tìm cộng đồng, nạn nhân báo cáo lạm dụng, giáo dục và thông tin y tế, vận động thay đổi; trong khủng hoảng (đại dịch) công cụ trực tuyến giữ trường học, doanh nghiệp, gia đình kết nối. Không phải nguyên nhân chính vì chủ yếu khuếch đại khó khăn có nguyên nhân khác, nhưng cần điều tiết hợp lý.

8.text:
From antibiotics to smartphones, science and technology have changed almost every part of daily life, and opinions are divided as to whether they improve people's lives or cause problems. This essay will consider both perspectives before explaining my own opinion.

On the one hand, supporters argue that science and technology have raised living standards in health, communication and convenience. Vaccines and medical devices save lives, the internet and mobile networks connect people instantly, and machines make work and housework faster. A villager who consults a city doctor by video, for example, receives expert advice without travelling for hours. Advances in agriculture, transport and energy have reduced hunger and poverty and allowed people to live longer and more comfortable lives. Knowledge is more accessible than ever, which helps education and personal development, and technology creates new industries and careers.

On the other hand, critics point out that technology also causes problems. Automation can destroy jobs, factories and vehicles pollute the environment, weapons are more destructive, and personal data are collected on a huge scale, which threatens privacy. Many people feel overwhelmed by screens, notifications and constant connection, and it can reduce attention and face-to-face contact. Dependence on complex systems makes societies vulnerable when they fail, as in power cuts or cyber-attacks. Some argue that technology has also widened the gap between rich and poor, since the benefits are not shared equally.

In conclusion, both views have merit. Personally, I believe that science and technology improve life overall, but their harmful effects must be managed through regulation, education and responsible use.

Nâng mức sống về sức khoẻ, giao tiếp, tiện lợi: vaccine, thiết bị y tế cứu mạng; internet, mạng di động nối ngay; máy móc làm việc nhanh. Ví dụ dân làng hỏi bác sĩ thành phố qua video không phải đi hàng giờ. Nông nghiệp, vận tải, năng lượng giảm đói nghèo, sống lâu hơn, thoải mái hơn; kiến thức dễ tiếp cận hơn bao giờ hết; công nghệ tạo ngành nghề mới.

Công nghệ cũng gây vấn đề: tự động hoá phá việc làm; nhà máy, phương tiện ô nhiễm; vũ khí tàn phá hơn; dữ liệu cá nhân thu thập quy mô lớn đe doạ riêng tư; choáng ngợp bởi màn hình, thông báo, giảm chú ý và tiếp xúc trực tiếp; phụ thuộc hệ thống phức tạp dễ tổn thương khi hỏng (mất điện, tấn công mạng); nới rộng khoảng cách giàu nghèo.
Cải thiện cuộc sống nhìn chung nhưng tác hại phải quản lý bằng điều tiết, giáo dục, dùng có trách nhiệm.

12.text:
Technology now shapes every industry, from farming to finance, and many governments see it as the key to prosperity. This essay will outline two principal benefits for a country that focuses on technology: a stronger economy and better public services.

First and foremost, a country that invests in technology becomes more productive and competitive. High-tech industries create well-paid jobs and exports, and digital tools help every business, from small shops to large factories, to work faster and reach more customers. A country that allows citizens to file taxes and vote online, for example, saves time and money for both government and residents. Technology also attracts investment and talented people, and it helps countries to create new products instead of competing only on low costs. Nations such as South Korea and Singapore have built prosperity by combining education with strong technology sectors.

In addition, technology improves public services and quality of life. Digital records allow hospitals to share information safely, online services reduce queues and paperwork, and data helps cities to manage traffic, energy and waste. A villager who consults a city doctor by video, for example, receives expert advice without travelling for hours. Farmers use sensors and satellite information to grow more with fewer resources, and online education reaches students who live far from good schools. Although technology requires investment, training and protection against misuse, such as privacy violations, a country that plans carefully can enjoy long-term gains. Governments should also ensure that everyone has access, so that the benefits are shared.

To sum up, focusing on technology brings clear benefits to a country, above all a stronger economy and better public services. For these reasons, it deserves sustained public support.

37.text:
Research laboratories, universities and observatories rarely make headlines, but their discoveries shape medicine, industry and daily life, and many countries invest heavily in them. This essay will outline two principal benefits for a country that focuses on science and research: economic growth and solutions to national and global problems.

First and foremost, a country that invests in science and research becomes more productive and competitive. High-tech industries create well-paid jobs and exports, and the knowledge produced by universities leads to new products and companies. Many of today's industries, from the internet to biotechnology, grew from basic research that had no immediate commercial aim. A country that supports research can also attract talented scientists and investors from abroad, and benefit from patents and spin-off businesses. South Korea and Germany show how sustained investment in research and engineering can support strong, innovative economies.

In addition, science provides the knowledge to solve major problems. Basic research produces medicines, vaccines, materials and clean energy technologies, and scientists help governments to deal with disease, climate change and food shortages. Research also trains highly skilled people who work in industry, teaching and government, and it raises the general level of education. During a pandemic, for example, a country with strong research capacity can develop tests and vaccines more quickly and protect its population. Although research is expensive, uncertain and slow to deliver, and not every project succeeds, the long-term returns have been very large. Governments should therefore give researchers stable funding and freedom to pursue ideas.

To sum up, focusing on science and research brings clear benefits to a country, above all economic growth and the ability to solve major problems. For these reasons, it deserves sustained public support.

Nước đầu tư khoa học và nghiên cứu năng suất, cạnh tranh hơn; ngành công nghệ cao việc làm lương tốt và xuất khẩu; tri thức đại học dẫn đến sản phẩm, công ty mới. 117.text:
New inventions, from electric cars to artificial intelligence, appear every year, and governments are keen to encourage innovation. This essay will outline two principal benefits for a country that focuses on technological innovation: new industries and jobs, and improved efficiency and quality of life.

First and foremost, technological innovation creates new industries, jobs and exports. A company that develops a better battery or a new medical device can grow into a major employer, and clusters of such firms attract suppliers, researchers and investors. A country that becomes known for efficient batteries, for instance, can sell them to many others. Innovative countries earn a reputation that attracts talented workers and international investment, and they are less dependent on exporting raw materials or low-cost goods. Start-up companies also create competition, which pushes older firms to improve. Societies that encourage experimentation tend to adapt more quickly to economic change.

In addition, innovation improves efficiency and quality of life. New technologies in health, transport and energy reduce costs, save time and cut pollution. A farm that switches from flooding its fields to drip irrigation, for example, can grow the same crop with far less water. Innovations such as online banking, ride-sharing and telemedicine make services cheaper and more convenient, and clean technology helps countries to meet environmental goals. Although innovation brings risks, such as job changes and ethical questions, and not every idea succeeds, governments can reduce these through education, retraining, and sensible regulation. A society that invests in innovation prepares itself for the challenges of the future.

To sum up, technological innovation brings clear benefits to a country, above all new industries and jobs and a better quality of life. For these reasons, it deserves sustained public support.

34.text:
Robots weld cars, software sorts parcels and self-service machines process payments, and many people think that automation has improved people's lives. I agree with this view, since automation removes dangerous and repetitive work and makes goods cheaper, although it also creates difficulties that need to be managed.

To begin with, automation removes dangerous and repetitive work and makes goods cheaper. Machines handle heavy lifting, hazardous chemicals and repetitive assembly, raising productivity and lowering prices. A robot that welds car parts, for example, protects workers from fumes and produces more consistent results. Factories that use automation have fewer accidents, and products such as cars, phones and food are more affordable than they would otherwise be. Automation in offices removes tedious tasks like data entry, so that people can concentrate on more interesting work involving judgement and creativity. Hospitals use automated systems to deliver supplies and process test results, which frees nurses to care for patients.

Furthermore, automation has created new jobs in design, maintenance, programming and services, and it has allowed people to enjoy shorter working hours and more leisure than previous generations. However, workers whose jobs disappear need retraining and support, and automation may widen inequality if the gains go only to owners of machines. Towns that depended on a single factory can suffer badly. Governments and employers should therefore invest in education and retraining, provide support for those who lose jobs and ensure that the benefits are shared through fair taxation and wages. When managed well, automation improves living standards for most people.

In conclusion, I agree that automation has improved people's lives, because it makes work safer and goods cheaper, provided that those who lose out are supported.

Nhà máy ít tai nạn; xe, điện thoại, thực phẩm rẻ hơn; văn phòng loại việc nhập liệu chán nên tập trung việc thú vị cần phán đoán, sáng tạo; bệnh viện dùng hệ thống tự động giải phóng y tá chăm bệnh nhân.

54.text:
In little more than a decade, smartphones have become part of daily life for billions of people, and many think that smartphone use has improved people's lives. I agree with this view, since smartphones put communication, information and services in everyone's pocket, although they have costs that users should manage.

To begin with, smartphones put communication, information and services in everyone's pocket. People can contact family, find directions, bank, shop and call for help from one device. A traveller who is lost in an unfamiliar city, for example, can find the way, translate a menu and call a taxi with one phone. Students can access encyclopaedias and lessons, workers can answer messages while away from the office, and farmers in remote villages can check weather forecasts and market prices. In emergencies, a phone can call for help or share location, which has saved many lives. Camera, maps, music and payments in one device would have required many gadgets in the past.

Furthermore, smartphones have widened access to services for people who were previously excluded, such as mobile banking in places without branches and health advice in remote areas. However, there are real costs. Constant notifications and social media can be addictive and distracting, sleep and concentration may suffer, and personal data may be collected and misused. Children and teenagers are especially vulnerable to pressure and bullying. Users can reduce these risks by setting limits, turning off notifications, protecting privacy and putting the phone aside during meals and before bed. The value of a smartphone therefore depends on how sensibly it is used.

In conclusion, I agree that smartphones have improved people's lives, because they provide convenience, information and safety, provided that people use them in moderation.

356.text:
Calendars, messaging tools, note-taking apps and project boards are now part of working life, and many people think that mobile apps have improved productivity. I agree with this view to a large extent, since apps save time by organising, automating and connecting work, although they can also distract.

To begin with, mobile apps save time by organising, automating and connecting work. Calendars, task lists, shared documents and messaging remove delays and paperwork. A team that uses a shared calendar and chat app, for example, can arrange a meeting in minutes instead of exchanging dozens of emails. Apps allow people to work from anywhere, reply to customers instantly and scan documents or sign contracts without printing. Scheduling tools, expense trackers and reminders reduce errors and forgotten tasks, and automation tools handle repetitive actions such as sending invoices. For small businesses and freelancers, affordable apps provide capabilities that once required an office and staff.

Furthermore, apps help individuals to manage their own time and learning. Fitness trackers, language lessons and budgeting tools encourage regular habits, and collaborative platforms allow colleagues in different countries to work together. However, productivity does not rise automatically. Notifications and endless features can distract and reduce real output, and constant availability may blur the line between work and rest, leading to stress. Research suggests that people check their phones many times a day and take time to refocus afterwards. Productivity improves when people choose a few tools, switch off unnecessary alerts and set times for deep work. Used with discipline, apps are a major help.

In conclusion, I agree that mobile apps have improved productivity to a large extent, because they save time and reduce effort, provided that users manage distractions carefully.

Làm việc từ bất kỳ đâu, trả lời khách ngay, quét tài liệu, ký hợp đồng không in; công cụ lập lịch, theo dõi chi phí, nhắc nhở giảm sai sót; tự động hoá việc lặp lại như gửi hoá đơn; doanh nghiệp nhỏ, freelancer có khả năng trước đây cần văn phòng và nhân viên.

Giúp cá nhân quản lý thời gian và học: theo dõi sức khoẻ, bài học ngôn ngữ, ngân sách khuyến khích thói quen; nền tảng cộng tác cho đồng nghiệp nhiều nước. Giới hạn: năng suất không tự tăng: thông báo, tính năng vô tận gây xao nhãng, giảm đầu ra thật; luôn sẵn sàng làm mờ ranh giới làm việc và nghỉ, gây căng thẳng; người dùng kiểm tra điện thoại nhiều lần mỗi ngày, mất thời gian tập trung lại; chọn vài công cụ, tắt cảnh báo thừa, đặt giờ làm việc sâu.

265.text:
In cafes, trains and living rooms, people can be seen looking at screens instead of at one another, and opinions differ on whether technology reduces face-to-face interaction. This essay will consider both perspectives before explaining my own opinion.

On the one hand, supporters of this view argue that technology can reduce face-to-face contact. Time spent on screens can replace conversation, and people may prefer to text rather than meet. A family that scrolls through phones at dinner, for example, shares the same table but not the same conversation. Children who spend hours on games or videos may play less with friends, and workers who use messaging may avoid walking to a colleague's desk. Researchers have linked heavy social media use with loneliness, since online contact can feel less satisfying than real company. Habits such as checking phones during conversations also signal that the person present is less important than the device.

On the other hand, others point out that technology also helps people to meet. Messaging, video calls and social networks keep distant friends and relatives in touch, and people use apps to arrange gatherings, find groups with shared interests and organise events. Migrants and students living abroad can speak to their families every day. Online communities can reduce isolation for people with illnesses or unusual interests, who may not find others like them nearby. Many online friendships lead to meetings in person.

In conclusion, both views have merit. Personally, I believe that the outcome depends on how technology is used: when devices replace personal contact, relationships suffer, but when they support it, they can strengthen links between people.

analysis.type_vi: Discuss both views: công nghệ giảm tiếp xúc trực tiếp hay không

plan.think: Mở bài nêu hình ảnh (người nhìn màn hình thay vì nhìn nhau trong quán cà phê, tàu, phòng khách) rồi hai phe; ý kiến riêng: phụ thuộc cách dùng.

Thời gian màn hình thay trò chuyện, người ta thích nhắn tin hơn gặp. Ví dụ gia đình lướt điện thoại ở bữa tối cùng bàn mà không cùng cuộc trò chuyện. Trẻ chơi game, xem video hàng giờ ít chơi với bạn; nhân viên dùng nhắn tin tránh đến bàn đồng nghiệp; nghiên cứu liên hệ dùng mạng xã hội nhiều với cô đơn; kiểm tra điện thoại khi nói chuyện báo hiệu người trước mặt kém quan trọng hơn thiết bị.

Nhắn tin, cuộc gọi video, mạng xã hội giữ bạn bè và người thân xa liên lạc; ứng dụng để hẹn gặp, tìm nhóm cùng sở thích, tổ chức sự kiện; người di cư, sinh viên nước ngoài nói chuyện với gia đình mỗi ngày; cộng đồng trực tuyến giảm cô lập cho người bệnh hoặc sở thích khác thường; nhiều tình bạn trực tuyến dẫn đến gặp trực tiếp.
Kết quả phụ thuộc cách dùng: thiết bị thay tiếp xúc thì quan hệ tổn thương, hỗ trợ thì củng cố.

204.text:
With a single tap, an app can smooth skin, reshape a jaw or brighten eyes, and many feel that photo editing apps create unrealistic beauty standards. I agree with this view, since edited images make unrealistic appearances look normal, although awareness and rules can reduce the harm.

To begin with, photo editing apps make unrealistic images look normal. Filters smooth skin, change shapes and brighten features so well that edited faces seem real, and young people who compare themselves with them may feel dissatisfied with their own bodies. A teenager who edits every selfie to make her skin flawless, for example, may start to believe that her real face is unattractive. Because many images on social media are edited, often without any label, users see a stream of apparently perfect people and may assume that this is the standard. Studies have linked heavy use of such images to anxiety about appearance, low self-esteem and, in some cases, eating disorders and cosmetic surgery requests.

Furthermore, the pressure affects people of all ages and genders, and it can be reinforced by advertising and celebrities who use the same tools. Editing also changes the ideal over time, so that what is considered beautiful becomes increasingly narrow. However, the apps themselves are not entirely to blame, since people have long manipulated images with make-up and airbrushing. Some users employ filters for fun or creativity, and many people are aware that images are edited. Education about editing in schools, clear labels on altered advertising images and platforms that reduce the promotion of heavy filters can limit the damage. Encouraging people to value diversity and natural appearances also helps.

In conclusion, I agree that photo editing apps create unrealistic beauty standards, because they make edited looks seem normal, though education and honest labelling can reduce the harm.

analysis.type_vi: Agree/Disagree: ứng dụng chỉnh ảnh tạo chuẩn đẹp phi thực tế — agree

plan.think: Mở bài nêu khả năng (một chạm làm mịn da, thay hàm, làm sáng mắt) rồi agree + lý do + điều kiện (nhận thức và quy định giảm tác hại).

plan.step: 2. Lý do 1 — ảnh phi thực tế thành bình thường
plan.think: Bộ lọc làm mịn da, đổi hình dạng, làm sáng đặc điểm đến mức khuôn mặt chỉnh nhìn như thật; người trẻ so sánh với chúng thấy không hài lòng cơ thể. Ví dụ thiếu nữ chỉnh mọi ảnh tự chụp cho da hoàn hảo có thể tin gương mặt thật xấu. Nhiều ảnh mạng xã hội đã chỉnh, thường không nhãn, người dùng thấy dòng người dường như hoàn hảo, nghĩ là chuẩn; nghiên cứu liên hệ với lo lắng ngoại hình, tự trọng thấp, đôi khi rối loạn ăn uống và nhu cầu phẫu thuật thẩm mỹ.

Áp lực ảnh hưởng mọi tuổi, giới; củng cố bởi quảng cáo và người nổi tiếng; chuẩn đẹp ngày càng hẹp. Giới hạn: ứng dụng không hoàn toàn đáng trách vì người ta vẫn chỉnh ảnh bằng trang điểm, airbrush từ lâu; một số dùng bộ lọc cho vui, sáng tạo; nhiều người biết ảnh đã chỉnh; giáo dục về chỉnh sửa ở trường, nhãn rõ trên ảnh quảng cáo bị chỉnh, nền tảng giảm quảng bá bộ lọc nặng; khuyến khích trân trọng đa dạng và vẻ tự nhiên.
Agree vì làm diện mạo đã chỉnh có vẻ bình thường, giáo dục và nhãn trung thực có thể giảm tác hại.

75.text:
Genetically modified crops are grown in many countries and banned in others, and some believe that genetically modified food is beneficial. I largely agree, since modified crops can raise yields and improve nutrition, although careful regulation and honest labelling are essential.

To begin with, genetically modified food can be beneficial when it is regulated and tested. Modified crops can resist disease, survive drought and carry extra nutrients, which raises yields and reduces chemical use. A rice variety enriched with vitamin A, for example, could help to prevent blindness in children whose diet lacks it. Farmers who plant pest-resistant varieties use fewer pesticides, which protects both their health and the environment, and crops that tolerate poor soil or dry weather can provide food where traditional varieties fail. With the global population rising and climate change affecting harvests, technologies that increase output without clearing more land have clear value.

Furthermore, scientific reviews by major health organisations have found that approved modified foods are as safe to eat as their conventional equivalents. However, concerns should not be dismissed. Some people worry about long-term effects on health and ecosystems, the spread of modified genes to wild plants, and the control of seeds by a few large companies. Public trust is important, so governments should require independent testing, publish the results and label modified products so that consumers can choose. Support for small farmers and public research, instead of dependence on private companies, would also help to share the benefits. Where safety and fairness are ensured, modified food can be a valuable tool in the fight against hunger.

In conclusion, I largely agree that genetically modified food is beneficial, because it can increase food supplies and nutrition, provided that it is tested and regulated carefully.

plan.step: 2. Lý do 1 — lợi ích khi được kiểm nghiệm và điều tiết
plan.think: Cây biến đổi kháng bệnh, chịu hạn, mang thêm chất dinh dưỡng, tăng năng suất, giảm hoá chất. Ví dụ giống gạo bổ sung vitamin A có thể giúp ngăn mù ở trẻ thiếu trong chế độ ăn. Nông dân trồng giống kháng sâu dùng ít thuốc trừ sâu nên bảo vệ sức khoẻ và môi trường; cây chịu đất nghèo hoặc thời tiết khô cho lương thực nơi giống truyền thống thất bại; dân số tăng, khí hậu ảnh hưởng mùa vụ nên công nghệ tăng sản lượng không phá thêm đất có giá trị.

Đánh giá khoa học của các tổ chức y tế lớn thấy thực phẩm biến đổi đã được phê duyệt an toàn như loại thông thường. Giới hạn: lo ngại không nên gạt bỏ: ảnh hưởng dài hạn lên sức khoẻ, hệ sinh thái; gen lan sang cây dại; hạt giống bị vài công ty lớn kiểm soát; niềm tin công chúng quan trọng nên chính phủ yêu cầu kiểm nghiệm độc lập, công bố kết quả, dán nhãn; hỗ trợ nông dân nhỏ và nghiên cứu công.
Largely agree vì tăng nguồn cung lương thực và dinh dưỡng, với điều kiện kiểm nghiệm và điều tiết cẩn thận.
